title: APT: Atomic Physical Transitions for Causal Video-Language Understanding
abstract: arXiv:2606.18586v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Physical events are not understood by their names alone, but by the causal state changes that compose them. A clip-level label such as "bounce" can be correct while hiding the process that makes the event physically valid, from support loss and contact onset to rebound and settling. To make this hidden process explicit, we introduce Atomic Physical Transitions (APTs): minimal, temporally localized state changes that bind a visible cue to an active physical mechanism and before/after dynamical regimes. An APT chain represents a video as an ordered causal transition sequence rather than a single aggregate event label: event labels tell what happened; APT chains explain why it happened. To make APTs learnable by VLMs, we construct mixed-source APT data from human annotations and simulator ground truth, covering 14 transition types across contact, gravity, friction, and rotation/stability, with 27,303 timed instances over 1,246 tri

translated_title: APT：用于因果视频-语言理解的原子物理转变
translated_abstract: 物理事件的理解不能仅凭其名称，而要通过构成它们的因果状态变化来实现。诸如“弹跳”这样的片段级标签可能是正确的，但却隐藏了使事件在物理上成立的过程——从失去支撑、接触发生，到反弹和稳定。为了使这一隐藏过程显性化，我们引入了原子物理转变：最小化的、时间上局部化的状态变化，它将可见线索与活跃的物理机制以及转变前后的动力学状态绑定在一起。APT链将视频表示为有序的因果转变序列，而非单一的聚合事件标签：事件标签告诉我们发生了什么，而APT链解释了为什么会发生。为了使视觉语言模型（VLM）能够学习APT，我们从人类标注和模拟器真值构建了混合来源的APT数据，涵盖接触、重力、摩擦以及旋转/稳定性等14种转变类型，包含27,303个带时间标注的实例，分布于1,246个……
tldr: 该论文提出原子物理转变（APT）这一新表示方法，将视频中的物理事件分解为最小化的因果状态变化序列，使视觉语言模型能够理解物理事件“为什么”发生，而不仅仅是“发生了什么”。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes Atomic Physical Transitions (APTs), a new representation that decomposes physical events in videos into minimal, temporally localized causal state-change sequences, enabling vision-language models to understand why physical events happen rather than just what happened.
